boundary_rationale: The fifth poem opens without an acrostic but with a three-imperative chain: זְכֹ֤ר יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Lam.5.1, byte tier) is followed in the same verse by a ketiv-qere pair, הביט הַבִּ֖יטָה (oshb:Lam.5.1, byte tier; the inventory's own K/Q note here), both readings meaning look or regard, and then by a third imperative carrying its own vav prefix, וּרְאֵ֥ה (oshb:Lam.5.1, byte tier); the full verse, זְכֹ֤ר יְהוָה֙ מֶֽה הָ֣יָה לָ֔נוּ הביט הַבִּ֖יטָה וּרְאֵ֥ה אֶת חֶרְפָּתֵֽנוּ (oshb:Lam.5.1, byte tier), reads “Remember, Yahweh, what has come on us. Look, and see our reproach.” (web:Lam.5.1). As a petition imperative to the divine name, the remember-form stands in 2 verses, here and at web:Lam.3.19 (skeleton tier), the third member of its 3-verse bare-token census being the negated third-person perfect at web:Lam.2.1; the look-form stands in 2 verses as a bare token and in 4 under the single-letter prefix test, at web:Lam.1.11, web:Lam.2.20, web:Lam.3.63 and web:Lam.5.1 (skeleton tier at both digits). The communal voice then catalogs loss across 5:2-5:10 without a further direct address to YHWH: inheritance surrendered, “We are orphans and fatherless. Our mothers are as widows.” (web:Lam.5.3), water and wood bought at a price, foreign servitude, inherited guilt, and at the group's own close, עוֹרֵ֨נוּ֙ כְּתַנּ֣וּר נִכְמָ֔רוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י זַלְעֲפ֥וֹת רָעָֽב (oshb:Lam.5.10, byte tier), “Our skin is black like an oven, because of the burning heat of famine.” (web:Lam.5.10) — the catalogue's 1st-plural form closing before a four-verse gap at Lam.5.11-Lam.5.14 (1st-plural sweep: 0 of those 4 verses), where a run of third-plural verbs on bare plural human-group subjects opens at 5:11.

The group turns from external causes to the community's own confession, נָֽפְלָה֙ עֲטֶ֣רֶת רֹאשֵׁ֔נוּ — the crown fallen from our head (oshb:Lam.5.16, byte tier) — “The crown has fallen from our head.” (web:Lam.5.16), the sixth of this span's eight verses.
